chunks: O you who believe, do not make friends with those who have suffered the anger of God by having become despondent of the life to come like those unbelievers who are despondent of those who are in the graves.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ‌ الْقُبُورِ: The people of the graves / The dead
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter / The life to come
key_terms.غَضِبَ‌ اللَّهُ‌ عَلَيْهِمْ: Those upon whom God has wrath

ai.seo_question: Who are the people described as despairing of the Hereafter in Surah Al-Mumtahanah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a directive for political and spiritual distinctiveness (Tawalli and Tabarri), specifically warning against forming deep alliances with those who have lost hope in resurrection, such as the Jews of Medina or the polytheists of Mecca. The comparison to 'owners of the graves' highlights their certainty in death's finality, mirroring the disbelievers' denial of the Hereafter, thus serving as a criterion for identifying true believers' allies and enemies.
